cues.en: This is a video about things like cars, phones, and light bulbs,
cues.zh: 这是一期关于汽车、手机和灯泡等东西的视频，

cues.en: and an actual conspiracy
cues.zh: 以及一个真实的阴谋

cues.en: that made them worse.
cues.zh: 它让这些东西变得更糟了。

cues.en: This video was sponsored by NordVPN.
cues.zh: 本期视频由 NordVPN 赞助。

cues.en: More about them at the end of the video.
cues.zh: 视频结尾会详细介绍他们。

cues.en: I am outside Livermore Fire Station Number 6. And in here, they have the longest continuously on light bulb in the world. It has been on for a hundred and twenty years
cues.zh: 我现在在利弗莫尔第6消防站外面。这里面有一盏世界上连续点亮时间最长的灯泡。它已经亮了一百二十年

cues.en: since nineteen o one. There it is. Yeah. That's it. It's not even connected to a light switch,
cues.zh: 从1901年开始。就是它。没错。就是这盏。它甚至没接灯开关，

cues.en: but it does have a backup battery and generator.
cues.zh: 但它有备用电池和发电机。

cues.en: So the big question is, how has this light bulb lasted so long? It was manufactured by hand not long after commercial light bulbs were first invented.
cues.zh: 所以关键问题是，这盏灯泡怎么能用这么久？它是在商用灯泡刚发明不久后手工制造的。

cues.en: And yet, it has been running for over a million hours,
cues.zh: 然而，它已经运行了一百多万个小时，

cues.en: way longer than any light bulb today is meant to last.
cues.zh: 远远超过今天任何灯泡的设计寿命。

cues.en: A while back, a friend of mine told me this story that someone had invented a light bulb that would last forever years ago, but they never sold it because an everlasting light bulb makes for a terrible business model. I mean you would never have any repeat customers and eventually you would run out of people to sell light bulbs to.
cues.zh: 前阵子，我一个朋友跟我讲了个故事，说多年前有人发明了一种永久耐用的灯泡，但一直没卖，因为永久灯泡是个糟糕的商业模式。我是说，你永远不会有回头客，最终你会把能卖灯泡的人全卖光。

cues.en: I thought this story sounded ridiculous.
cues.zh: 我觉得这故事听着太荒唐了。

cues.en: If you could make an everlasting light bulb then everyone would buy your light bulb over the competitors
cues.zh: 如果你能造出永久灯泡，那所有人都会买你的而不是竞争对手的

cues.en: So you could charge really high prices, make a lot of money even if demand would eventually dry up. I just couldn't imagine that we had better light bulbs in the past and then intentionally
cues.zh: 所以你可以定很高的价格，赚很多钱，即使需求最终会枯竭。我就是无法想象我们过去有更好的灯泡，然后故意

cues.en: made them worse.
cues.zh: 把它们做得更糟。

cues.en: But it turns out I was wrong,
cues.zh: 但事实证明我错了，

cues.en: at least sort of.
cues.zh: 至少从某种程度上说。

cues.en: Inventing a viable electric light was hard. I mean, is the typical incandescent design which just involves passing electric current through a material making it so hot that it glows.
cues.zh: 发明一种可行的电灯很难。我的意思是，典型的白炽灯设计就是让电流通过一种材料，使其热到发光。

cues.en: You know, less than 5% of the electrical energy comes out as light. The other 95%
cues.zh: 你知道，只有不到5%的电能转化为光。其余95%

cues.en: is released as heat.
cues.zh: 以热的形式释放。

cues.en: So these are really heat bulbs which give off a little bit of light as a byproduct.
cues.zh: 所以这些其实是发热灯泡，只是附带产生一点光。

cues.en: You know, the temperature of the filament can get up to 2,800
cues.zh: 你知道，灯丝的温度可以达到2800

cues.en: Kelvin.
cues.zh: 开尔文。

cues.en: That is half as hot as the surface of the sun.
cues.zh: 那是太阳表面温度的一半。

cues.en: At temperatures like those, most materials melt. And if they don't melt So cool. They burn,
cues.zh: 在这样的温度下，大多数材料都会熔化。如果它们不熔化，那还好。它们会燃烧，

cues.en: which is why in the eighteen forties, Warren de la Rue came up with the idea of putting the filament in a vacuum bulb so there's no oxygen to react with.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么在19世纪40年代，Warren de la Rue想出了把灯丝放在真空灯泡里的主意，这样就没有氧气与之反应。

cues.en: Thomas Edison had made a bulb with a cotton thread filament
cues.zh: Thomas Edison用棉线灯丝制作了一个灯泡

cues.en: that lasted fourteen hours.
cues.zh: 持续了14个小时。

cues.en: Other inventors created bulbs with platinum filaments or other carbonized materials
cues.zh: 其他发明家创造了用铂丝或其他碳化材料做灯丝的灯泡

cues.en: and gradually the lifespan of bulbs increased.
cues.zh: 灯泡的寿命逐渐增加。

cues.en: The filaments changed from carbon to tungsten,
cues.zh: 灯丝从碳变成了钨，

cues.en: which has a very high melting point. And by the early nineteen twenties, average bulb lifetimes were approaching two thousand hours with some lasting twenty five hundred hours.
cues.zh: 钨的熔点非常高。到20世纪20年代初，灯泡的平均寿命接近2000小时，有些能持续2500小时。

cues.en: But this is when lifetimes
cues.zh: 但就在这时，寿命

cues.en: stopped getting longer and started getting shorter.
cues.zh: 不再变长，反而开始变短。

cues.en: In Geneva, Switzerland, just before Christmas nineteen twenty four, there was a secret meeting of top executives from the world's leading light bulb companies.
cues.zh: 在瑞士日内瓦，就在1924年圣诞节前，世界领先的灯泡公司的高管们举行了一次秘密会议。

cues.en: Philips, International General Electric,
cues.zh: Philips、International General Electric，

cues.en: Tokyo Electric, Osram from Germany, and The UK's Associated Electric among others.
cues.zh: Tokyo Electric、德国的 Osram，以及英国的 Associated Electric 等公司。

cues.en: They formed what became known as the Phoebus Cartel,
cues.zh: 它们组成了后来众所周知的 Phoebus 卡特尔，

cues.en: named after Phoebus, the Greek god of light.
cues.zh: 名字取自希腊光明之神 Phoebus。

cues.en: There, all these companies agreed to work together to help each other by controlling the world's supply of light bulbs.
cues.zh: 在那里，所有这些公司同意携手合作，通过控制全球灯泡供应来互相帮助。

cues.en: In the early days of the electrical industry, there had been lots of different small light bulb manufacturers.
cues.zh: 在电气工业的早期，曾有许多不同的小型灯泡制造商。

cues.en: But by now,
cues.zh: 但到那时，

cues.en: they had largely been consolidated into these big corporations,
cues.zh: 它们已基本整合成这些大公司，

cues.en: each dominant in a particular part of the world.
cues.zh: 各自在世界某个特定地区占据主导地位。

cues.en: The biggest threat they all faced was from longer lasting light bulbs.
cues.zh: 它们共同面临的最大威胁，来自寿命更长的灯泡。

cues.en: For example, in 1923,
OSRAM sold 63,000,000
cues.zh: OSRAM 卖出了 6300 万

cues.en: light bulbs, but the following year, they sold only 28,000,000.
cues.zh: 只灯泡，但第二年只卖出了 2800 万只。

cues.en: Light bulbs were lasting too long, eating into sales.
cues.zh: 灯泡寿命太长了，侵蚀了销量。

cues.en: So all the companies in the cartel agreed to reduce the lifespan of their bulbs to one thousand hours,
cues.zh: 于是卡特尔中的所有公司同意把灯泡寿命缩短到一千小时，

cues.en: cutting the existing average almost in half.
cues.zh: 几乎把当时的平均寿命砍掉了一半。

cues.en: But how could each company ensure that the other companies would actually follow the rules and make shorter lasting light bulbs? After all, it would be in each of their individual interests to make a better product to outsell the others.
cues.zh: 但每家公司怎么能确保其他公司真的遵守规则、生产寿命更短的灯泡呢？毕竟，做出更好的产品来超越对手，符合每一家各自的利益。

cues.en: Well, to enforce the thousand hour limit, each of the manufacturers had to send in sample bulbs from their factories,
cues.zh: 为了强制执行一千小时的上限，每个制造商都必须从自家工厂送交样品灯泡，

cues.en: and they were tested on big test stands like this one.
cues.zh: 并像这样在大测试台上进行测试。

cues.en: If a bulb lasted significantly longer than a thousand hours, well then the company was fined.
cues.zh: 如果灯泡寿命明显超过一千小时，公司就会被罚款。

cues.en: If a bulb lasted longer than three thousand hours,
cues.zh: 如果寿命超过三千小时，

cues.en: well, the fine was 200 Swiss francs for every thousand bulbs sold.
cues.zh: 每售出一千个灯泡，罚款就高达200瑞士法郎。

cues.en: And there are records of these fines being issued to companies.
cues.zh: 而且有记录证明这些罚单确实开给过各家公司。

cues.en: But how do you make a worse light bulb in the first place?
cues.zh: 但话说回来，一开始你怎么才能把灯泡故意造得更烂？

cues.en: Well, same engineers who had previously been tasked with extending the lifespan
cues.zh: 那些曾经负责延长灯泡寿命的工程师，

cues.en: now had to find ways to decrease it. So they tried different materials, different shaped filaments, and thinner connections.
cues.zh: 现在却不得不去想办法缩短寿命。于是他们尝试了不同材料、不同形状的灯丝，以及更细的导线。

cues.en: And if you look at the data, they were successful.
cues.zh: 从数据来看，他们成功了。

cues.en: Ever since the formation of the cartel, the lifespan of light bulbs steadily decreased.
cues.zh: 自该卡特尔成立以来，灯泡的寿命便持续稳步下降。

cues.en: So that by 1934,
cues.zh: 以至于到了1934年，

cues.en: the average lifespan was just twelve hundred and five hours.
cues.zh: 平均寿命只剩下1205个小时。

cues.en: And just as they had planned, sales increased for cartel members by 25%
cues.zh: 正如他们预想的那样，卡特尔成员的销量增长了25%，

cues.en: in the four years after 1926.
cues.zh: 这仅仅是在1926年之后的短短四年里。

cues.en: And even though the cost of components came down, the cartel kept prices virtually unchanged,
cues.zh: 尽管零部件成本下降了，卡特尔却让价格基本保持不变，

cues.en: so they increased their profit margins.
cues.zh: 从而提高了他们的利润率。

cues.en: So did people know that the light bulb companies were conspiring together to make their products worse?
cues.zh: 那当时的人们知道灯泡公司在暗中勾结、故意把产品做烂吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 并不知道。

cues.en: The Phoebus Cartel claimed that its purpose was to increase standardization
cues.zh: Phoebus Cartel 声称其目的是为了提高标准化

cues.en: and efficiency of light bulbs. I mean, they did establish this screw thread as standard. You can find it on virtually all light bulbs around the world now.
cues.zh: 和灯泡的能效。不过，他们确实把这种螺纹接口确立为了标准，如今全世界几乎所有灯泡上都能见到它。

cues.en: But all evidence points to the cartels being motivated by profits and increased sales,
cues.zh: 但所有证据都表明，卡特尔是受利润和销售增长的驱动，

cues.en: not by what was best for consumers.
cues.zh: 而不是为了消费者的最佳利益。

cues.en: So one of the reasons this light bulb has lasted so long is because it was made before the cartel era.
cues.zh: 所以这只灯泡能用这么久，原因之一是它是在卡特尔时代之前制造的。

cues.en: Another reason is because the filament has always been run at low power, just four or five watts.
cues.zh: 另一个原因是灯丝一直以低功率运行，只有四五瓦。

cues.en: It was meant to be a night light for the fire station to provide just enough light so that firemen wouldn't run into things at night.
cues.zh: 它原本是消防站的夜灯，提供刚好足够的光线，让消防员在夜间不会撞到东西。

cues.en: And the fact that it was always on reduced the thermal cycling of the filament and components, limiting the stress caused by thermal expansion and contraction.
cues.zh: 而它一直开着，减少了灯丝和组件的热循环，限制了热胀冷缩造成的应力。

cues.en: The Phoebus cartel was initially planned to last at least until 1955,
cues.zh: Phoebus 卡特尔最初计划至少持续到 1955 年，

cues.en: but it fell apart in the nineteen thirties.
cues.zh: 但它在 20 世纪 30 年代就瓦解了。

cues.en: It was already struggling due to outside competition and noncompliance amongst some of its members, but the outbreak of World War two is really what finished it off.
cues.zh: 它当时已经因为外部竞争和部分成员的不遵守而举步维艰，但真正终结它的是第二次世界大战的爆发。

cues.en: So this cartel was dead
cues.zh: 所以这个卡特尔已经死了

cues.en: but its methods survived to this day.
cues.zh: 但它的手段延续至今。

cues.en: There are lots of companies out there that intentionally shorten the lifespan of their products.
cues.zh: 有很多公司故意缩短产品的使用寿命。

cues.en: It's a tactic known now as planned obsolescence.
cues.zh: 这种策略现在被称为计划性淘汰。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: was actually the subject of Casey Neistat's first viral video all the way back in 2003.
cues.zh: 实际上是 Casey Neistat 早在 2003 年第一个爆火视频的主题。

cues.en: Thank you for calling Apple. My name is Ryan. May I have your name
cues.zh: 感谢致电 Apple。我叫 Ryan。请问您是哪位

cues.en: Casey. Alright. What seems to be the issue today? I have an iPod that I bought about eighteen months ago and and the battery is dead on it. Mhmm. Eighteen months? Okay. It's past its year, which basically means for, it'll... There'll be a charge of $255
cues.zh: Casey。好的。今天有什么问题？我有一台大约十八个月前买的 iPod，电池坏了。嗯。十八个月？好的。已经超过一年了，基本上意味着……会收取 255 美元

cues.en: plus a mailing fee to send it to us to read... To refurb it,
cues.zh: 外加邮寄费，寄给我们来修……来翻新，

cues.en: to correct it. But at that price, you know, you might as well go get a new one.
cues.zh: 来修复它。但按这个价格，你知道，你还不如去买个新的。

cues.en: This video got millions of views in a time before YouTube or social media, and it spawned a class action lawsuit,
cues.zh: 这段视频在 YouTube 或社交媒体出现之前的时代就获得了数百万次观看，还引发了一场集体诉讼，

cues.en: which Apple settled out of court.
cues.zh: Apple 最终庭外和解。

cues.en: But it didn't stop the company from practicing planned obsolescence.
cues.zh: 但这并没有阻止该公司继续践行计划性淘汰。

cues.en: After an iOS update in 2017,
cues.zh: 2017 年的一次 iOS 更新之后，

cues.en: users of older iPhones found apps loading significantly slower or the device shutting down altogether.
cues.zh: 旧款 iPhone 用户发现应用加载明显变慢，甚至设备直接关机。

cues.en: Apple said they throttled performance to protect the battery of older devices and increase their longevity.
cues.zh: Apple 表示他们限制性能是为了保护旧设备的电池、延长其使用寿命。

cues.en: Of course, that wouldn't be an issue if the battery were replaceable.
cues.zh: 当然，如果电池可更换，这就不是问题了。

cues.en: In a series of lawsuits that concluded in 2020,
cues.zh: 在 2020 年落幕的一系列诉讼中，

cues.en: Apple was fined or reached settlements to pay hundreds of millions of dollars.
cues.zh: Apple 被罚款或达成和解，支付了数亿美元。

cues.en: Undoubtedly,
cues.zh: 毫无疑问，

cues.en: this amount pales in comparison to the extra revenue they generate by limiting the lifespan of their products.
cues.zh: 与限制产品寿命所带来的额外收入相比，这笔钱微不足道。

cues.en: But some would argue that planned obsolescence isn't just about greed,
cues.zh: 但有人认为，计划性淘汰不只是贪婪，

cues.en: but that it's also good for everyone. During
cues.zh: 它对所有人都有好处。在

cues.en: the Great Depression in the nineteen thirties,
cues.zh: 20 世纪 30 年代的大萧条时期，

cues.en: when as much as a quarter of Americans were out of work, an American real estate broker Bernard London proposed
cues.zh: 当时多达四分之一的美国人失业，美国房地产经纪人 Bernard London 提出

cues.en: mandatory planned obsolescence as a way to get people back to work and lift America out of the depression.
cues.zh: 强制性的计划性淘汰，以此让人们重返工作岗位，把美国拉出大萧条。

cues.en: He wrote, I would have the government assign a lease of life to shoes and homes and machines when they are first created
cues.zh: 他写道，我会让政府在鞋子、房屋和机器刚被制造出来时，就为其指定一个使用寿命，

cues.en: and they would be sold and used within the term of their existence definitely known by the consumer.
cues.zh: 它们将在消费者明确知晓的存续期限内被出售和使用。

cues.en: After the allotted time had expired, these things would be legally dead and would be controlled by the duly appointed governmental agency and destroyed
cues.zh: 规定的期限一到，这些东西就会在法律上消亡，由正式任命的政府机构接管并销毁

cues.en: if there is widespread unemployment.
cues.zh: 如果出现大规模失业。

cues.en: Now this might sound like a wild fringe idea,
cues.zh: 这听起来可能像是个疯狂的边缘想法，

cues.en: but people were clearly afraid of being put out of work by technological progress and products that were too good.
cues.zh: 但人们显然害怕被技术进步和过于优秀的产品夺走工作。

cues.en: There was even a popular Oscar nominated film about it. This is the man in the white suit from 1951.
cues.zh: 甚至还有一部获得奥斯卡提名的热门电影讲的就是这个。这是1951年的《白衣男子》。

cues.en: It's about a scientist who invents the perfect fiber. It won't stain or break or fray. I think I've succeeded in the copolymerization
cues.zh: 讲的是一个科学家发明了完美的纤维。它不沾污、不破裂、不磨损。我想我已经成功实现了共聚

cues.en: of amino acid residues and carbohydrate molecules,
cues.zh: 氨基酸残基和碳水化合物分子，

cues.en: both containing ionic groups.
cues.zh: 两者都含有离子基团。

cues.en: It's really perfectly simple. The Academy Award nomination was for best screenplay.
cues.zh: 真的很简单。奥斯卡提名是最佳编剧奖。

cues.en: I kid you not.
cues.zh: 我没开玩笑。

cues.en: Anyway,
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: everyone is initially excited about our hero's scientific discovery.
cues.zh: 一开始大家都对我们主角的科学发现感到兴奋。

cues.en: He makes a suit out of the thread, and it has to be white because the fiber is so stain resistant it can't even be dyed.
cues.zh: 他用这种线做了一套西装，必须是白色的，因为这种纤维太抗污了，甚至没法染色。

cues.en: But this is when trouble strikes. The factory owners realize they won't be able to sell as much of this thread because it's so durable,
cues.zh: 但麻烦就在这时来了。工厂主意识到这种线太耐用了，他们卖不了那么多，

cues.en: and the workers worry it'll put them out of a job. Why can't you
cues.zh: 工人们则担心这会让他们失业。你们为什么不能

cues.en: scientists
cues.zh: 科学家们

cues.en: leave things alone?
cues.zh: 别管闲事？

cues.en: What about my bitter washing when there's no washing to do?
cues.zh: 没衣服可洗的时候，我的洗衣苦活怎么办？

cues.en: This is when you get the climactic scene where factory workers and factory owners
cues.zh: 这时就到了高潮场景，工厂工人和工厂主

cues.en: team up to chase down the scientist to destroy him and his invention.
cues.zh: 联手追捕科学家，要毁掉他和他的发明。

cues.en: And believe it or not, this movie may have been inspired by real events.
cues.zh: 信不信由你，这部电影可能取材于真实事件。

cues.en: In the nineteen forties, the synthetic fiber nylon replaced silk in stockings,
cues.zh: 20世纪40年代，合成纤维尼龙取代丝绸被用于制作长袜，

cues.en: It was so durable that the products became an overnight sensation.
cues.zh: 它极其耐穿，产品一夜之间风靡全国。

cues.en: There were literal riots when women tried to get their hands on them.
cues.zh: 女性为了抢购甚至引发了名副其实的骚乱。

cues.en: When the manufacturers realized they had made the product too good, they didn't destroy the fiber,
cues.zh: 当制造商意识到产品质量好过头时，他们并没有销毁这种纤维，

cues.en: but they did follow the example of the Phoebus cartel.
cues.zh: 但他们确实效仿了 Phoebus 卡特尔的做法。

cues.en: They instructed their engineers and scientists to find ways to weaken the product to shorten its lifespan so people would have to buy more.
cues.zh: 他们指示工程师和科学家想办法削弱产品强度、缩短使用寿命，好让人们买得更频繁。

cues.en: Now it seems like consumers are finally fighting back against planned obsolescence.
cues.zh: 如今，消费者似乎终于开始反抗这种“计划性报废”了。

cues.en: In the European Union and in over 25 states in The US, there's proposed legislation to enshrine the right to repair.
cues.zh: 在欧盟以及美国超过25个州，都提出了确立“维修权”的立法提案。

cues.en: These laws would force manufacturers to make it easier to repair their products. They would have to provide information and access to parts so you could replace a battery or fix a cracked screen at a third party repair shop without voiding your warranty.
cues.zh: 这些法律将强制制造商降低维修难度。他们必须提供维修资料和零部件渠道，让你在第三方维修店换电池或修碎屏时，不至于失去保修资格。

cues.en: So if the right to repair does become law, does that mean artificial obsolescence will be gone for good?
cues.zh: 那么，如果维修权真的正式立法，人为报废就会彻底终结吗？

cues.en: Sadly,
cues.zh: 很遗憾，

cues.en: no. Because there is one last thing manufacturers can use to make their products obsolete,
cues.zh: 并不会。因为制造商还有最后一招能让产品被淘汰，

cues.en: which is you.
cues.zh: 那就是你。

cues.en: Henry Ford released the first mass market car, the Model T in nineteen o eight. And he envisioned it like a workhorse,
cues.zh: 1908年，Henry Ford 推出了首款面向大众市场的汽车 Model T。他将其设想为任劳任怨的“老黄牛”，

cues.en: an affordable tool that wouldn't wear out, a bit like the everlasting light bulb. In 1922 Ford said, we want the man who buys one of our cars never to have to buy another. We never make an improvement that renders any previous model obsolete.
cues.zh: 一件价格亲民且永不磨损的工具，有点像那盏永远不灭的灯泡。1922年 Ford 曾说：“我们希望买我们车的人永远不必再买第二辆。我们绝不会做出任何让旧款车型被淘汰的改进。”

cues.en: But by 1920,
cues.zh: 但到了1920年，

cues.en: of American families already owned a car. Nearly everyone that could afford one had one.
cues.zh: 的美国家庭已经拥有了汽车。几乎所有买得起车的人都买了一辆。

cues.en: And that same year, there was a small economic downturn driving down sales for both Ford and General Motors.
cues.zh: 同一年发生了一场轻度经济衰退，导致 Ford 和 General Motors 的销量双双下滑。

cues.en: DuPont, the chemical and paint company, took over the controlling share in General Motors
cues.zh: 化工与涂料公司 DuPont 收购了 General Motors 的控股权，

cues.en: and they started experimenting with painting cars different colors.
cues.zh: 并开始尝试给汽车涂上不同的颜色。

cues.en: Up until then, Henry Ford had said, you could have whatever color you like so long as it's black.
cues.zh: 在这之前，Henry Ford 曾说过：你可以要任何你喜欢的颜色，只要它是黑色的。

cues.en: It took a couple years of testing, but in 1924,
cues.zh: 经过几年的测试，到了1924年，

cues.en: GM released their first cars in different colors. And soon after, they introduced a trick that feels very familiar now.
cues.zh: GM 推出了首批彩色汽车。不久之后，他们又玩出了一个如今大家都很熟悉的套路。

cues.en: Each new year, they would introduce cars in different colors.
cues.zh: 每年他们都会推出全新配色的车型。

cues.en: The goal wasn't just to make Ford's model t look outdated, but to make their own cars feel outdated every year, encouraging customers to trade in their old cars for shiny new ones.
cues.zh: 其目的不仅是让 Ford 的 Model T 显得过时，更是让自己上一年的车也显得落伍，从而促使客户以旧换新、换上光鲜亮丽的新车。

cues.en: Years later, GM's head of design Harley Earl candidly discussed his role in creating what he called dynamic obsolescence.
cues.zh: 多年后，GM 设计主管 Harley Earl 坦诚地谈到了他在开创所谓的“动态报废”理念中所扮演的角色。

cues.en: Our big job is to hasten obsolescence.
cues.zh: “我们的主要任务就是加速过时淘汰。”

cues.en: the average car ownership span was five years. Now, which was 1955,
cues.zh: 一辆车的平均持有时间是五年。而现在（指1955年），

cues.en: it is two years. When it is one year, we will have a perfect score.
cues.zh: 变成了两年。要是能缩短到一年，那我们就拿到满分了。”

cues.en: By the time he said this, General Motors was the most valuable company in the world and it sold half of all vehicles purchased in The US every year.
cues.zh: 当他说出这番话时，General Motors 已经是全球市值最高的公司，每年在美国售出的汽车有一半都来自他们。

cues.en: These days, the world's most valuable company, Apple, seems to have copied directly out of this playbook. I mean, styles every year, check. New special colors every year, check.
cues.zh: 如今，全球市值最高的公司 Apple 似乎直接照搬了这套套路。我是说，每年换款式，有；每年出新特别配色，有。

cues.en: Marginal technological improvement,
cues.zh: 微小的技术改进，

cues.en: check. I mean is this useful innovation or just a gimmick?
cues.zh: 有。我是说，这是有用的创新，还是只是噱头？

cues.en: The inspiration for General Motors and hence for Apple comes from fashion
cues.zh: General Motors、进而 Apple 的灵感来自时尚界

cues.en: where real innovation is all but impossible.
cues.zh: 而在时尚界，真正的创新几乎是不可能的。

cues.en: So the only way to make people feel the urgency to get out there and buy is to create styles that last but one season.
cues.zh: 所以，要让人感到非买不可，唯一办法就是推出只流行一季的款式。

cues.en: The trouble then is you run through these styles too quickly and then what are you supposed to do? Well, just recycle the styles from a few decades ago.
cues.zh: 但问题在于，你很快就把这些款式用完了，接下来怎么办？那就把几十年前的款式再拿出来循环一遍。

cues.en: The iPhone also shows this recycling trend. I mean, just look at the way the edges were initially rounded and then they were squared off and then they were rounded again and now they're squared off. And how much do you wanna bet that the iPhone 14 has rounded edges?
cues.zh: iPhone 也体现了这种循环趋势。看看边缘：先圆角，然后改成直角，然后又圆角，现在又直角。你信不信 iPhone 14 又是圆角？

cues.en: I think the point is that with design and styling there is no best.
cues.zh: 我觉得关键在于，设计和造型上没有最好。

cues.en: There's only different
cues.zh: 只有不同

cues.en: which is apparently enough to remind us that we don't have the latest and greatest and so we have to rush out and keep buying.
cues.zh: 而这显然足以提醒我们：自己没拥有最新最强的东西，于是赶紧冲出去继续买。

cues.en: The only type of obsolescence we should support is technological,
cues.zh: 我们唯一该支持的淘汰是技术性淘汰，

cues.en: which brings us back to the light bulb. You know, in the last twenty years, light bulbs have gone from incandescent,
cues.zh: 这就说回灯泡。过去二十年，灯泡从白炽灯

cues.en: which was basically unchanged for a hundred years, to compact fluorescent,
cues.zh: 白炽灯基本一百年没变，发展到紧凑型荧光灯，

cues.en: and now to LED.
cues.zh: 再到现在 LED。

cues.en: These use just a tenth the energy and can last anywhere from 10 to 50 times longer.
cues.zh: 这些灯泡的能耗只有十分之一，寿命却长达10到50倍。

cues.en: Yeah. That's pretty bright. So you're more likely to sell your house than to have to replace an LED bulb that you've installed inside it.
cues.zh: 是啊，确实很亮。所以你更可能先卖掉房子，而不是要更换装在里面的LED灯泡。

cues.en: So we finally reached the point of
cues.zh: 所以我们终于达到了这样一个阶段——

cues.en: what is essentially an everlasting light bulb.
cues.zh: 本质上就是永远不坏的灯泡。
